svg.text: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model structure, and the Plan B layout on this machine
40 layers · hidden size 5,120 · 4 hyper-connection residual streams · vocabulary 129,280 · context 1M (YaRN 16×, native 64K) · 763B parameters in total
Left bars: where the dense part / routed experts are:
Token embedding 129,280 × 5,120 (BF16) → copied into 4 residual streams; every layer then reads and writes all 4
Computed for every prompt token; each layer = attention + MoE (6 of 384 experts, plus 1 shared expert)
Ratio 2 · writes compressed KV and index keys · picks its own top-512
Ratio 2 · reads L2's compressed KV and L2's top-512
Ratio 2 · reads L2's compressed KV and L2's top-512

Ratio 2 · reads L2's compressed KV and L2's top-512

Ratio 2 · reads L8's compressed KV and L8's top-512
Ratio 2 · writes compressed KV and index keys · picks its own top-512
Ratio 2 · reads L14's compressed KV and L14's top-512

Ratio 2 · reads L14's compressed KV and L14's top-512
Ratio 2 · reads L14's compressed KV and L14's top-512
CED: prefill computes only tokens that later tokens can still see via the sliding window; fewer in later layers, only the last in L39
Ratio 1 · writes compressed KV shared by L20–39 · picks top-512 + blocks
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L20's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L20's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L20's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV · reselects top-512 in candidate blocks
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L24's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L24's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L24's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV · reselects top-512 in candidate blocks
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L28's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L28's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L28's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV · reselects top-512 in candidate blocks
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L32's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L32's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L32's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV · reselects top-512 in candidate blocks
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L36's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L36's top-512
Ratio 1 · reads L20's compressed KV and L36's top-512
Final RMSNorm → output head 5,120 × 129,280 (BF16) → logits for the next token
DSpark draft model: 3 layers × 128 experts (MXFP4, 7.4 GiB) for speculative decoding; tried here, not adopted
Inside one layer (a decoder layer as an example)
4 residual streams · hyper-connections mix 4 into 1; weights Sinkhorn-normalized (20 iterations)
After RMSNorm; 64 query heads, only 1 KV head (K = V, 512 dims)
q_a's output also feeds the sparse indexer
Sliding window: raw KV of last 128 tokens
Compressed KV: one row per r tokens
Indexer lets only the top-512 rows through
flash attention: 128 window rows + 512 compressed rows, one sink per head
Output projection: 8 low-rank groups (rank 1,024) → 5,120, back into the 4 residual streams
Hyper-connections mix again to form the input → RMSNorm
Routing: score 384 experts, pick 6, normalize weights, × 1.5
MXFP4, ~18.8 MB per expert, 7.2 GB per layer
1 shared expert: computed for every token
Weighted sum written back to the 4 residual streams
Only in layers 1 and 14: look up two large tables by n-gram hashes of the last 2–4 tokens
Each ~384M rows × 256 dims; 24 rows/token (3 lengths × 8 heads), gated into the residual stream
Score = Σ_h ReLU(q_h · k) · w_h; pick top-512 compressed rows among positions the query can see
Layer 20: 8 rows per block; picks 2,048 blocks by their highest score (newest block always kept)
Layers 24/28/32/36 reselect only in these blocks; others reuse the nearest index source's top-512
Layers 0–11 in full (experts 80.6 GiB + dense), layer 12 gate/up experts, first half of the head
Dense part of layers 12–39; experts of layers 12–21 (L12: down only); second half of the head
Expert cache 21.1 GB: hot experts of layers 22–39, ~1,170 slots
Decode cache misses: hot ones uploaded into the cache, the rest on the CPU, added a layer later
Two Engram tables, ~97 GiB (MXFP4), read via the page cache; whole batch prefetched before prefill
Sources: GGUF metadata (mxxm-t/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-GGUF), the official inference/model.py; layout and measurements on this machine: see the technical report and CLAUDE.md (2026-11-11)
